scope: PMX avatars containing both ordinary and D leg chains
observation: The audited model weighted D leg bones while the ordinary leg chain carried no vertex weight. Its upper body also had only two spine segments.
resolution: Map the weighted D chain and the existing spine segments; do not invent an upperChest mapping or transfer weights unnecessarily.
evidence: PMX inspector and conversion reports agree on the weighted D chain.
Final VRM has 53 human bones; the leg pose changed 38 sampled vertices with finite bounds.
regression: Local PMX audit plus three-vrm leg-pose screenshot and deformation samples
limitations: Mixed-weight rigs require separate rest-transform and weight-transfer review.

scope: PMX vertex morphs and groups referencing supported morphs
observation: The source had 162 vertex morphs and 14 group morphs; standard blinking depended on the groups.
resolution: Recursively bake group deltas into vertex shapes, reject cycles and unsupported morph types, and retain every source custom expression.
evidence: Final structural audit found 176 custom morphs and zero empty morphs.
All 13 standard expression probes activated geometry; mouth and blink screenshots were inspected.
regression: Local 162-vertex/14-group source replay with final morph inventory and face screenshots
limitations: Material, UV and bone morphs need explicit adaptation; count preservation alone does not prove every expression looks correct.

scope: VRM Add-on preset expression configuration
observation: Configured presets can retain existing bind entries when a script appends another mapping.
resolution: Clear each configured preset bind collection before writing the intended source shapes and weights.
evidence: Conversion uses clear before adding configured preset binds.
All 13 configured expression snapshots passed active-morph and maximum-weight checks at weight one.
regression: Replay the expression sweep and inspect mouth/eyelid screenshots
limitations: This does not automatically define suitable semantic expression mappings for a new model.

scope: PMX sphere mode 2 mapped to MToon matcap
observation: Two source materials used additive sphere maps; that mode is separate from the diffuse surface transparency.
resolution: Approximate additive sphere lighting with MToon matcap while deriving surface alpha from actual diffuse/texture alpha or explicit overrides.
evidence: The local conversion report records two matcap approximations.
Front, back, mouth and blink renders were inspected without whole-material transparency artifacts.
regression: Local MToon conversion replay and front/back visual inspection
limitations: Sphere lighting remains an approximation; multiply/subtexture sphere modes require a separate adaptation.

scope: Single-source-mesh embedded-texture VRM without morph-weight animations
observation: Facial targets allocated many zero-only layers on body and clothing primitives.
resolution: Split material parts, retain nonzero morphs, rebind expressions and first-person annotations, and compare decoded accessor values and image bytes.
evidence: Synthetic optimizer regression covers signed zero, node weights and both binding maps.
Local export decreased from 35655224 to 15629324 bytes; 263 retained accessors and nine images passed equality checks.
The optimized artifact passed actual three-vrm rendering and physics checks.
regression: node --test tests/optimizer.test.mjs; local final-artifact browser replay
limitations: Supported structure only; numerical equality here compares VRM exports, not original MMD physics or shading.

scope: VRM export and post-save object selection
observation: A successful exporter return or GLB load is insufficient evidence that avatar mesh data exists.
resolution: Enumerate the clean export scene, assert real mesh/material data and expected triangles, then validate finite geometry and actual vertex deformation.
evidence: Synthetic optimizer test rejects a skeleton-only container.
Final local audit verified 54313 triangles, eight materials and positive skinned mesh counts.
regression: node --test tests/optimizer.test.mjs tests/runtime.test.mjs; local final audit
limitations: Finite bounds and some moving samples still require visual review of hands, feet, clothing and expressions.

scope: Runtime report aggregation across a multi-frame simulation
observation: An object spread of the final snapshot could overwrite the accumulated nonfinite counter from earlier physics frames.
resolution: Merge transient and final counters explicitly; fail on either instead of inspecting only the final frame.
evidence: Synthetic test preserves two transient failures when the last snapshot is finite.
The corrected verifier completed the local 600-frame run with a total of zero nonfinite states.
regression: node --test tests/runtime.test.mjs; corrected local 600-frame replay
limitations: This catches numeric failures; it does not detect every collision or aesthetic defect.

scope: Chromium three-vrm runtime acceptance
observation: The viewer collected console errors, but the original acceptance check only rejected a subset of console messages.
resolution: Treat console errors and shader/context failures as failed verification and require all standard expression and pose evidence.
evidence: Synthetic tests reject shader errors, missing expressions, null bounds and nondeforming poses.
The corrected local replay completed with empty browser error and console arrays.
regression: node --test tests/runtime.test.mjs; corrected local browser replay
limitations: Warnings are preserved for inspection; not every warning is automatically fatal.

scope: Per-conversion maintenance of this skill
observation: Repeated observations should not create duplicate entries, and a changed observation should not silently overwrite a previous conclusion.
resolution: Record stable verified IDs with evidence and limitations, make identical replays a no-op, and require explicit replacement for corrections.
evidence: Recorder tests cover no-op duplicates, explicit revisions and retention of extra context.
Tests reject missing evidence and common private absolute paths while permitting source URLs.
regression: node --test tests/lessons.test.mjs
limitations: Schema and path checks are assistance only; the agent must review truth, scope and the full publish diff.

scope: Local comparison viewer with a restricted LoadingManager URL resolver
observation: An initial resolver accepted the selected VRM URL but rejected blob URLs created internally by GLTFLoader for embedded images, causing missing textures and MToon colorSpace errors.
resolution: Allow same-origin blob URLs and inline data resources before resolving selected external file paths; continue rejecting unselected external resources.
evidence: Both startup-argument and browser-file-input loads of the final VRM completed with all embedded images.
The corrected comparison page had no page or console errors during camera, exposure, export and mobile checks.
regression: Actual embedded-texture VRM replay through both example and file-input routes; inspect the console and rendered result.
limitations: This validates the pinned GLTFLoader/three-vrm combination, not arbitrary external-resource VRM files.

scope: Browser directory selection for PMX models with local textures
observation: Selecting a folder provides webkitRelativePath values while PMX textures can use backslashes or encoded paths; basename lookup would be ambiguous when subfolders reuse image names.
resolution: Normalize separators and encoded paths, resolve the complete relative path, permit only unique case-insensitive fallback, and fail explicitly on missing or ambiguous textures.
evidence: Synthetic tests cover Chinese paths, encoded spaces, Windows separators, duplicate basenames, ambiguous case and traversal rejection.
A real selected MMD folder with two PMX variants loaded correctly, and the intended normal variant could be selected.
regression: node --test tests/comparison.test.mjs; real browser folder-input replay with PMX variant selection.
limitations: Textures outside the selected folder must be included by choosing a suitable parent folder; do not silently fetch them from arbitrary locations.

scope: Bilingual MMD/VRM comparison viewer with already loaded GPU resources
observation: Translating static controls alone leaves dynamic loading, error, geometry and PNG captions in the previous language; rebuilding the viewer would also discard model and camera state.
resolution: Store status and pose translation keys with parameters, refresh displayed text in place, and translate export captions at export time. Preserve the original technical diagnostics and model filenames.
evidence: Browser replay switched Chinese and English after loading both real models; root UUIDs and camera positions/targets remained identical.
Loading summaries, triangle statistics, error messages, canvas accessibility labels and actual PNG captions used the selected language.
URL override, saved selection and English default checks passed; English screenshots at desktop and 390-pixel width were inspected.
regression: node --test tests/viewer-publish.test.mjs; actual two-model browser replay with language switches and bilingual PNG downloads
limitations: Model filenames and low-level dependency diagnostics retain their original text; mobile viewport checks do not establish real-device performance.

scope: Static comparison viewer deployed under a project URL subdirectory
observation: The local comparison server can expose explicitly selected example models; copying its runtime configuration into a public site would publish model locations or assets. Root-relative asset URLs also fail under a project subdirectory.
resolution: Build a fixed set of browser assets, write an empty example manifest, reject unexpected existing output files, and resolve page assets and configuration relative to the app module. Load selected models through local browser File/blob APIs.
evidence: The static build contained exactly six allowed files, no machine paths in bundled JavaScript, and null MMD/VRM examples; an injected model file caused the next build to fail explicitly.
A browser loaded the static site from a project subdirectory, then rendered real PMX and embedded-texture VRM files with 54313 triangles per side.
The browser network record contained only GET requests for the page, stylesheet, bundled script and empty manifest, with no model requests or uploads; no page or console errors occurred.
regression: node --test tests/viewer-publish.test.mjs; static subdirectory browser replay and network/console inspection
limitations: A local static replay does not prove an external deployment succeeded; verify the actual published URL after deployment.

scope: PMX materials with a nonzero sphere mode and texture index -1
observation: A valid PMX retained sphere mode 2 without a sphere texture reference; the generic helper incorrectly rejected it as an unsupported active material.
resolution: Record inactive mode flags and continue. Reject unsupported sphere modes only when a texture index is actually referenced.
evidence: The real source retained 42524 triangles and 50 custom morphs after conversion.
The final avatar passed all thirteen standard expressions, deformation probes and 600 finite simulation frames; front/back and face screenshots were inspected.
The updated shared converter was replayed successfully on the same source, including humanoid hierarchy preflight.
regression: Local source replay through scripts/convert_pmx.py and final-artifact browser/structure checks; npm test
limitations: Active multiply and subtexture sphere modes still require deliberate adaptation; a missing active image remains an error.

scope: Audited PMX vertex, bone and diffuse material morph adaptations
observation: A source reused vertex morph names for bone morphs. Other controls changed material opacity rather than geometry; four material controls were empty source separators.
resolution: Preserve type/index identity and reverse name mappings. Bake supported bone effects from a controlled evaluated pose, map supported material operations to color binds with alpha-capable materials, and record empty controls, unsupported channels and clamps.
evidence: One source preserved 30 vertex, two baked bone and one material controls after disambiguating repeated names.
Another source preserved 61 vertex, 27 baked bone and 15 material controls, including four documented empty separators.
Material expression names and bind counts were audited separately; visible neutral/blink/mouth frames and additional control snapshots were captured.
regression: Local source morph inventory, materialColorBind count audit, runtime standard and additional expression probes
limitations: Bone deltas are rest-pose approximations. Unsupported shader/UV effects are not recreated; numeric activity does not prove every custom expression is artistically equivalent.

scope: PMX rigs whose human-bone names exist but ancestry is incompatible with VRM
observation: Legs descended from the mapped spine through zero-weight cancellation helpers, and shoulders descended from the neck. T-pose and export returned CANCELLED despite populated mappings.
resolution: Inspect ancestry and weights; reparent audited helpers without changing rest positions, map the appropriate weighted hips bone, refresh VRM Add-on candidates, and report explicit humanoid errors before export.
evidence: VRM Add-on reported 43 hierarchy errors before repair and zero after the tested hip/leg-helper/shoulder repairs.
The repaired component retained all 111347 triangles and passed arm/leg deformation and 600 finite simulation steps.
regression: Local VRM Add-on error_messages before/after repair plus successful shared-converter preflight replay
limitations: This is not permission to reparent every similarly named rig; constraints, weighted transforms and actual ancestry still require inspection.

scope: Three rigged FBX packages with separate game material JSON
observation: Y-up local bone coordinates were already rotated to Z-up by the importer object transform. A second rotation made the avatar sideways, while inherited white emission washed out diffuse textures. Numeric verification still passed.
resolution: Update the dependency graph and inspect world coordinates, preserve consistent transforms for rig and meshes, rebuild material channels from the supplied metadata, and explicitly reset unwanted emission.
evidence: All three corrected final avatars were inspected in front/back and neutral/blink/mouth renders.
Source triangle counts 30639, 54692 and 54161 and mesh layouts 7, 7 and 12 were retained.
Each corrected avatar passed thirteen standard expression checks, skinning deformation and 600 finite simulation steps.
regression: Actual FBX import/export replay, exported material inspection and final three-vrm renders
limitations: Game-specific lightmaps, eye/shadow shaders and packed masks are only partly represented; no secondary physics was inferred from absent configuration.

scope: PBR restoration from an audited outfit material package
observation: A shader-node green-channel inversion appeared in Blender but the exported normal image remained unchanged. DITHERED surface mode alone also exported BLEND for a source masked material.
resolution: Bake channel conversion into a separate derived texture, connect exporter-supported image/Normal Map nodes, and check decoded embedded image values. Express the alpha threshold explicitly and verify exported MASK.
evidence: Before baking, exported normal pixels equaled the source and the intended green inversion had maximum error 255.
After baking, decoded embedded green inversion error was zero and red/blue channel error was zero for the inspected normal image.
Exported normal and metallic-roughness textures were present, both intended cutout materials used MASK, and final PBR front/back renders were inspected.
regression: Decoded source-versus-embedded pixel comparison, glTF material inspection and local PBR runtime replay
limitations: Channel-byte checks do not establish the original engine normal convention, custom lighting, detail layers or subsurface appearance; convention assumptions and unsupported channels remain documented.

scope: Batch conversion of complete avatars, headless outfit components and multi-mesh assets
observation: A headless outfit had a complete humanoid bone map and zero expressions. Other numerically passing exports were sideways, over-emissive or cropped by a fixed-height QA camera.
resolution: Inspect actual source geometry and final screenshots; label component capabilities explicitly. Keep strict expression defaults for normal avatars, document any scoped local exception, preserve unsupported multi-mesh optimizer inputs unchanged, and frame current model bounds.
evidence: The batch delivered nine complete avatars with thirteen checked standard expressions and one explicitly labeled headless component with no invented expressions.
All ten retained source triangles, unchanged source hashes, and separate runtime/structure and visual-review records.
Multiple-mesh/no-expression outputs used byte-identical passthrough with an explicit unoptimized report.
regression: Per-artifact capability inventory, final checksum audit, runtime checks and actual front/back/available face inspection
limitations: Software rendering and finite simulation are not target-app/device acceptance, full cloth collision equivalence or a newly granted model license.

scope: An editable converted avatar with accessories isolated by audited material face sets
observation: A requested no-accessory variant needed permanent geometry removal while the original file and the character's existing shape keys, weights and expressions remained usable.
resolution: Use the source accessory-hiding material control to confirm the affected material scope, remove only its face sets in a separate Blender copy, track surviving vertex identities, compare every retained shape coordinate and vertex weight, and remove the now-obsolete accessory-only expression. Record the intended triangle reduction instead of weakening full-source triangle checks.
evidence: The local variant removed 4460 of 46966 triangles; the final file contained 42506 triangles and no primitives assigned to either accessory material.
All retained shape-key coordinates and weights matched the source using preserved vertex identities. Thirty-two custom expressions, 54 human bones and 18 spring chains remained.

The optimized 8152316-byte final passed thirteen standard expression probes, skinning deformation and 600 finite simulation frames. Front/back, blink and mouth renders were inspected, and original Blender/VRM hashes remained unchanged.
regression: Local material-scope audit, surviving-vertex shape/weight comparison, explicit removed-triangle audit and final three-vrm render replay
limitations: Material names alone are not proof of an isolated accessory; shared materials or shared topology require finer selection. Unused rig bones were retained to preserve hierarchy. This local adaptation is not a new automatic mode of the published converter.

scope: PMX imports containing the complete MMD Tools SDEF storage-key set
observation: An import contained 33 authored vertex morphs plus three SDEF storage shape keys. Binding every Blender shape key exposed the storage keys as 36 public expressions with unintended body-wide deltas.
resolution: Compare the imported names with PMX morph records before expression setup. Exclude only the complete known SDEF storage-key set from the export mesh, retain the original import, and reject authored reserved-name collisions, unknown extras and incomplete helper sets.
evidence: The repaired shared converter replay retained 389622 triangles, all 33 authored custom expressions, 13 standard presets, 15 embedded images and 53 human bones.
The final file contained no SDEF storage targets or expressions, and passed final runtime, pose, 600-frame finite simulation and screenshot inspection.
Five dependency-free Python regression tests and all nineteen existing Node tests passed.
regression: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'; npm test; actual PMX conversion and final three-vrm rendering
limitations: Standard VRM linear blend skinning approximates source SDEF. Removing importer storage is not evidence of exact SDEF deformation equivalence, and unknown helper types still require investigation.

scope: Audited weighted auxiliary arm bones that share the mapped arm rest segment but are siblings driven by MMD IK
observation: Two weighted sleeve/upper-arm followers were attached beneath the shoulders rather than the mapped arms. Removing their IK constraints without reconnecting them would leave that geometry behind during humanoid arm motion.
resolution: Confirm the source IK, weights, coincident rest pivots and aligned segments. In this scoped case, parent each follower beneath its mapped arm while retaining rest transforms and weights, then verify the exported hierarchy and actual posed geometry.
evidence: The final left and right followers influenced 4752 and 5094 exported vertices respectively.
Both followers remained direct children of their mapped arms; their arm-relative matrices differed by less than 1e-5 between T-pose and idle while world transforms changed.
Front, back and raised-arm screenshots were inspected; standard expression, arm/leg deformation and 600-frame runtime checks passed.
regression: Local source IK/rest-segment audit followed by final three-vrm follower-weight, hierarchy, relative-transform and raised-arm screenshot checks
limitations: Reparenting is not a general replacement for multi-target IK, twist distribution or nonlinear cloth constraints. Review each follower relationship before adapting other rigs.

scope: Audited opaque PMX accessories promoted to MToon BLEND to retain material-opacity controls
observation: At neutral alpha 1, the converted accessory and earrings appeared dark and lost visible texture because their transparent backface/outline rendering did not write depth.
resolution: Run a same-model depth-write and outline A/B before changing source textures. In the local adapter, explicitly enable MToon transparentWithZWrite for the audited originally opaque materials, then re-export and inspect neutral and off states. Keep the original export and record residual visibility.
evidence: The depth-write A/B restored the accessory texture and yellow earrings without changing source images.
The final exported file retained 30922 triangles, 46 geometry custom expressions, 9 material controls and 13 responding standard expressions; 600 simulation frames remained finite.
The accessory-off control removed its textured body but left a faint contour; that limitation is recorded instead of claiming complete geometry removal.
regression: Local three-vrm neutral/depth-write/opaque/no-outline A/B, final Blender re-export, standard expression and material-control screenshots, source/hash and optimizer invariants
limitations: This is a scoped local adapter fix, not a universal BLEND default or a claim that all opacity, layering and sphere-map controls are equivalent. Test partial transparency and occlusion for each target runtime.

scope: Read-only comparison of existing VRM 0 library/lab variants against a newly converted VRM 1 avatar
observation: The smaller file used more render calls; an enhanced baseline with extra wink morphs still had empty standard wink bindings. Rotating the VRM 0 scene did not alone normalize its arm-pose rotation basis. Sparse samples also missed some localized morph motion.
resolution: Preserve baseline hashes, normalize orientation and poses, render with controlled conditions, inspect effective preset bindings and full referenced morph data when sparse samples are inconclusive. Separate file size, source morph counts, geometric triangles, outline overhead and scene draw calls. Keep failed capability checks distinct from completed comparison captures.
evidence: An 11.08 MB, 30922-triangle conversion rendered with 56 calls and 59265 triangles including outlines; the 80.36 MB baseline rendered 59413 triangles in 5 calls under the same scene.
Both existing files had empty left/right blink preset bindings; only the lab variant exposed a working surprised preset. Additional wink target names did not fix the embedded presets.

The VRM 0 pose basis was corrected and standing/face images were visually inspected; both baseline hashes remained unchanged. Full accessor checks found real localized motion where sparse samples reported zero.
regression: Per-file GLB/hash/preset/accessor audit, controlled three-vrm VRM 0/1 capture, actual standing/face screenshot review and render-counter inspection
limitations: Embedded presets do not represent application-side remapping. Scene counters and software rendering do not establish mobile FPS, target-application acceptance or a universal visual-quality ranking.

scope: An incomplete PMX package with garbled atlas filenames, two absent active ribbon maps and a UTF-16 credit sheet
observation: The initial audit stopped on five missing active texture references. Three corresponding face, hair and accessory atlases existed under corrupted filenames, while two ribbon maps were absent. The credit sheet was readable only after BOM-based UTF-16 decoding.
resolution: Preserve the original package and create a derived staging copy. Visually confirm atlas matches, remap only those references without altering image bytes, and keep separate original/derived hashes. For the two absent maps, explicitly retain the affected geometry and original diffuse RGBA without a texture, with the lost pattern and texture alpha documented. Keep the generic converter's missing-active-texture failure intact.
evidence: The staged import resolved three atlas paths; final face, hair, accessory and front/back UV appearance was inspected. All original package file hashes remained unchanged.
Two missing maps affected 2304 triangles, which remained in the final 107098-triangle avatar with the original half-transparent black material fallback.

The final 19.77 MB VRM retained 68 vertex morphs and 8 material controls, passed thirteen standard expression checks and 600 finite simulation frames, and was delivered with visible missing-texture and source-license notes.
regression: Local original/derived manifest comparison, staged import, final structural and runtime audit, front/back/face/material screenshot inspection and gallery link/hash validation
limitations: Visual atlas matching is a case-specific recovery, not an automatic encoding repair. Missing pattern and texture alpha were not reconstructed. MMD cloth and material controls remain approximations; successful conversion does not grant commercial or redistribution rights.

scope: Two PMX avatars with repeated material names and index-based face ranges or material morphs
observation: Repeated source names become unique Blender material names, conflicting with the converter's name assertion and making name-only overrides ambiguous.
resolution: Assign unique names by source material index in a derived copy, keep a reverse map, and preserve all slot ordering and index-based references. Verify parsed source data before conversion rather than merging materials or bypassing the assertion.
evidence: Both parsed derived PMX files had identical vertices including weights, faces, bones, morphs, rigid bodies and joints; material properties differed only in names.
Final exports retained 19 and 28 material slots; the second retained all 24 material controls with verified binding counts.
Both final files passed their explicit expression capability profiles, posed geometry and 600-frame simulation checks, followed by screenshot and delivery hash/link inspection.
regression: Local original/derived PMX data comparison, ordered material inventory, VRM expression binding audit and actual final render replay
limitations: This is a local preprocessing recipe, not automatic merging or proof that all same-name slots have the same texture or behavior. Keep per-model mappings outside the public skill.

scope: A PMX containing opposite-winding copies of one face in a double-sided material
observation: The imported mesh retained 212054 triangles, while export contained 212053 and correctly failed the strict final audit.
resolution: Locate the exact source duplicate, compare counts by material and exported position multisets, verify both source and output are double-sided, and bind the scoped exception report to the final hash. Keep the shared triangle assertion unchanged.
evidence: The source pair used the same three vertex indices in opposite order in material slot 4; both source and VRM material flags were double-sided.
Only that material lost one instance. Its position-multiset difference was exactly the duplicate, with maximum nearest-position error below 1e-7 meters and explicit 1e-6 meter comparison precision.
All other material triangle counts were unchanged; the final file passed thirteen expression checks, 600 simulation frames and front/back/pose screenshot review.
regression: Local source-face identity and per-material triangle multiset comparison followed by hash-bound scoped final audit
limitations: This does not justify tolerating arbitrary count differences or claim exact shading equivalence. The generic auditor remains strict, and distinct surfaces require repair or explicit separate handling.

scope: A PMX with layered masked facial surfaces and global material-opacity controls
observation: Runtime numeric checks passed although promotion of OPAQUE and MASK materials to BLEND visually hid bangs, irises and the neutral mouth.
resolution: Use a same-model neutral/depth/cutout A/B. Restore MASK on the audited originally cutout face layers and transparent depth writing on the audited formerly opaque layers, retaining material controls with a documented cutoff-versus-smooth-fade tradeoff.
evidence: Opaque-layer depth writing restored bangs; adding the masked-layer cutout restored irises and neutral mouth without replacing images or removing the eye overlay.

The final re-export retained 50131 triangles, 15 authored vertex morphs, 9 source no-op bone controls and 24 material controls; eleven source-supported standard expressions and 600 finite simulation frames passed.

Final front/back/pose and face screenshots were inspected. A separate global fade replay reached zero opacity, visually hid the avatar, and restored exactly the original material state and neutral face.
regression: Local neutral/depth/cutout A/B, actual Blender re-export, final three-vrm expression/pose replay and global hide/restoration check
limitations: MASK uses a threshold instead of a smooth fade. Other clothing states and every legacy sphere/toon channel are not equivalent or visually accepted; this is not a universal transparency default.

scope: Audited UnityPackage FBX avatars with prefab blendshape overrides and named default animation curves
observation: The plain FBX import did not represent the selected prefab's authored clothed default. Some prefab shape-array sizes predated additional FBX shapes, while explicit index overrides still corresponded to named source controls.
resolution: Resolve assets through GUID metadata; inspect the actual ordered shape names and cross-check indexed defaults against named curves. Rebase the selected neutral geometry, retain remaining shape travel and add inverse reset controls. Preserve source data and distinguish untransferred prefab transforms, clips, menus and shader features.
evidence: Sixty-three named default blendshape bindings were checked against resolved source meshes and any matching indexed overrides; twenty-five active defaults were baked.
The final avatar retained seven meshes, 69229 triangles and 53 human bones. Thirteen standard expressions changed sampled geometry and were visually inspected with front/back and limb poses.

All 322 custom controls were activated and cleared in three-vrm with finite bounds and zero sampled geometry restoration error. Of these, 296 had nonzero geometry targets; no-op controls were explicitly listed.
The original archive and extracted asset/meta hashes remained unchanged. Unity menu and animation playback were not claimed as transferred.
regression: Local isolated Blender conversion, metadata cross-check, glTF binding/accessor audit, complete custom-control reset replay and rendered face/pose review
limitations: Renderer-ID mapping was audited for this package, not inferred from array lengths. Fixed baseline rebasing is not a universal wardrobe converter, and the original Unity shader/transform behavior was not fully reproduced.

scope: Separate local sparse-only optimization of an uncompressed seven-mesh VRM 1 export
observation: The single-source-mesh optimizer intentionally rejected this structural scope, but dense morph storage could be reduced without splitting or merging meshes.
resolution: Use a scoped adapter to replace eligible morph accessor storage with sparse data while preserving target indices and zero targets. Repack only referenced buffer views and prove every accessor's numerical equivalence, image byte equality and unchanged scene/material/VRM structures before rendering the final artifact.
evidence: Export size decreased from 111496216 to 88854796 bytes with 1135 accessors numerically equal and seven embedded images byte-identical; signed-zero normalization was counted.
Meshes, nodes, skins, materials, expressions and spring definitions were structurally unchanged, retaining 69229 triangles and 322 custom bindings.
The optimized artifact passed thirteen standard-expression renders, limb deformation checks, all custom-control restoration checks and finite secondary-motion replay.
regression: Local raw-versus-sparse numerical and structural comparison followed by browser load, expression/reset and secondary-motion verification
limitations: This adapter is not the bundled optimizer and does not extend its single-mesh contract. It does not prove source-renderer equivalence, support compressed geometry, or establish mobile performance.

scope: A six-segment tail and multi-chain hair in a locally converted UnityPackage avatar, tested with three-vrm
observation: A previous 600-frame check showed finite nonzero local spring rotations, but the owner still observed a rod-like tail and weak hair. Hips-centered stored simulation state suppressed response to body movement; identical-motion baseline tail peaks were about 1.0 to 1.85 degrees per joint.
resolution: Isolate the center effect with an identical-motion A/B, then tune root-to-tip tail stiffness and drag and distinguish bangs from other hair. The local revision omitted centers on hair/tail only, retained other chains, synchronized and reopened the editable project, and inspected a rendered movement/settling sequence.
evidence: At the same 60 fps body/head test, six tail joints reached about 37.75 to 63.16 degrees of peak local rotation; median peak hair rotation increased from 3.82 to 22.38 degrees.
Normal and gentle body motion plus six seconds of settling remained finite at 30, 60 and 120 fps; final-second tail-tip speed stayed below 0.8 mm/s.

Eight rear-oblique motion frames showed segment bending and settling without obvious tail/body intersection in those views; 13 standard expressions and all 322 custom-control resets passed on the final file.
regression: Replay identical body/head drivers against immutable baseline and final files, measure local rotations and settling, inspect animation/time samples, and reopen the synchronized Blender file.
limitations: Per-model tuning and a specific motion profile, not universal thresholds or equivalence to Unity PhysBones. No exhaustive collision or target-device acceptance. World-space springs require reset on teleport, and passive springs do not create autonomous wagging.

scope: A local multi-mesh sparse-storage adapter for an uncompressed embedded-image VRM with an explicit audited extension set
observation: The first sparse-storage pass still retained 531 orphan accessors because its bufferView reachability walk included every accessor, even those no primitive, skin or animation referenced.
resolution: Enumerate actual accessor references in primitive attributes, indices and targets, skin inverse-bind matrices and animation sampler input/output. Remap live accessor indices before pruning unreachable views and repacking aligned binary data. Reject unaudited extensions; preserve referenced zero targets and their target indices.
evidence: Removed 531 orphan accessors and 531 exclusive views; retained 604 live accessors with exactly identical decoded bytes.
All seven embedded 4K images remained byte-identical. Semantic comparison after reversing accessor-index remapping preserved meshes, nodes, skins, materials, expressions and other audited structures.

File size fell from 88.85 MB to 63.79 MB by storage compaction and 63.78 MB after separately changing physics JSON. Final runtime retained seven meshes, 69229 triangles, 13 standard expressions and 322 custom controls.
regression: Decode and compare every retained accessor, compare image bytes and semantic references, validate bounds and expression restoration in the final runtime, and retain the original export as fallback.
limitations: The public optimizer still has its one-source-mesh contract; the local multi-mesh adapter is not a universal extension-aware garbage collector. Download size decreases without reducing texture GPU memory. Physics changes must be audited separately from storage invariants.

scope: A user-requested downward tail with an upward-hooked tip, plus more responsive hair on a multi-mesh VRM avatar
observation: The previous spring revision was stable but its straight neutral tail did not match the requested J silhouette. Lowering drag aggressively caused excessive folding. Weight inspection also showed the tail root influenced an outfit mesh, so rotating every tail bone would alter clothing.
resolution: Preserve the shared attachment root, author the curve on downstream rest bones, bake the tail mesh to the new pose while keeping UVs/weights/topology, and then tune motion around the resulting neutral shape. Inspect side-view rest and settling renders, and compare identical body/head drivers with a close-up for hair.
evidence: The authored neutral tail descends through its middle and rises about 9.16 cm from the low point to the tip; the settled side view retains the hook.

Blender polygons, triangulation, UVs and weights remained identical. The exporter produced seven extra split vertices after normal deformation; all triangle-corner UV/color/skin identities matched, and other mesh/morph/image/material/expression data were unchanged.

Normal and gentle movement with six seconds of settling remained finite at 30/60/120 fps. Final 13 standard expressions and all 322 custom-control resets passed; eight side-motion frames and eight hair-closeup frames were visually inspected.
regression: Replay previous/final files with identical motion and cameras, verify neutral and recovered silhouette, compare editable topology and per-corner export attributes, verify non-target mesh/rest/inverse-bind invariants, and reopen the final Blender file.
limitations: This is an intentional art-direction edit and a scoped local replay, not a lossless shape conversion, exact Unity PhysBone transfer, universal force preset, exhaustive collision test or owner/target-device acceptance.

scope: Local adaptation of a PMXExporter MToonLike shader with base, emission and normal images packed in horizontal thirds
observation: Plain color-map conversion produced black hair strips. Source shader offsets identified three channel regions; two hair materials had U coordinates beyond the base-color third and sampled the emission region.
resolution: Inspect shader equations and actual UV ranges. Crop each channel without resizing, restore the divided U coordinate, and bind separate repeating base/emission/normal maps using the source channel factors. Preserve source files and record that fixing cross-channel tiling intentionally changes raw PMX appearance.
evidence: All 48 exported channel bindings matched the intended crop pixel hashes and dimensions.
258 geometry and morph attribute comparisons passed; U multiplied by three with zero measured error, and other attributes plus inverse binds remained identical.
Final runtime retained 53976 triangles, 54 human bones, 57 custom controls including one empty source control, and 25 spring chains; standard expression and pose screenshots were inspected.
Original ZIP and all 37 extracted files retained their hashes; before/after renders confirmed removal of the black hair strips.
regression: Local shader and UV audit, exact crop-to-export RGBA comparison, accessor comparison, standard-expression/custom-reset verification, and face/pose/movement screenshot inspection
limitations: Model-scoped adapter, not a generic atlas detector. Source shader lighting and tangent-space normal interpretation remain MToon approximations. Per-channel repeat intentionally repairs overflowing source UVs; no shader-identical rendering or target-device acceptance claim.

scope: A modular UnityPackage avatar assembled from body, costume and tail FBX components with an optional hidden coat
observation: JavaScript Number rounded signed 64-bit fileIDs. Raw FBX meshes also omitted nested prefab shape defaults, a tail scale, eye rotations and the authored hidden state of an optional coat.
resolution: Keep fileIDs exact; obtain FBX renderer and transform IDs, ordered shapes and local transforms using an isolated minimal Unity audit project. Follow source references and nested overrides, compare shared full rest matrices, distinguish q and -q, and bake verified changes into every shape and the rest skeleton. Preserve excluded components in the source.
evidence: Unity returned 1032 object/component records; the adapter resolved a sparse nested renderer override using the instance/source ID XOR relation and the FBX renderer table.

Three assembled rigs retained 19 meshes, 124868 triangles and 53 humanoid mappings. Tail scale and eye rotations were baked; the optional coat stayed excluded according to its explicit inactive state.
Source ZIP, UnityPackage, all extracted asset bytes and metadata hashes were unchanged. Final standard expressions, 592 custom-control resets and 30/60/120 fps spring probes passed.
regression: Replay source-ID resolution without floating-point conversion, compare authored defaults and shared rest matrices, verify source hashes, geometry counts, standard expression views and exact custom-control restoration.
limitations: Scoped local adapter, not a generic Modular Avatar builder. Source scripts were not executed; menu, constraint, interaction, collision and shader equivalence are not claimed. Four-weight runtime adaptation is separately measured and documented.

scope: A humanoid avatar with an authored frown baked into its neutral face and independent source vowel shapes
observation: Vowel shapes changed vertices and passed a nonzero-motion check, but the additive frown baseline nearly closed the ou and oh mouths in rendered output.
resolution: Bind the existing inverse frown target together with the affected phoneme and positive/surprised presets. Keep the authored frown for neutral and do not reset unrelated baselines.
evidence: Before/after face sheets showed open, distinguishable ou and oh after releasing the conflicting baseline.
All 13 standard expression renders were inspected; all 592 custom controls remained finite and returned to exactly the sampled baseline.
The final editable scene reopened successfully; only eight preset recipes gained the inverse-baseline binding, with source shapes retained.
regression: Compare neutral and every affected vowel/emotion image, verify nonzero geometric motion and clearing restoration against the final artifact hash.
limitations: Model-specific expression composition rule. A nonzero displacement test alone is insufficient, and source baseline shapes should not all be canceled indiscriminately.

scope: A Unity procedural analog clock shader with an MSDF atlas used by an avatar accessory
observation: Binding the atlas directly as base color displayed colored data artifacts instead of a clock face.
resolution: Read the source sampling equations and material parameters; decode the MSDF median and coverage, then bake the analog dial at a documented static time into a transparent image for MToon.
evidence: The adapter generated a 1024 square RGBA dial at 10:10:30 and preserved the original shader, texture atlas and material metadata.
The final accessory render no longer displayed the original colored atlas artifacts. Final VRM loads, expression checks and body poses remained valid.
Storage compression preserved every resulting embedded image byte; the bake itself is recorded as a separate material conversion.
regression: Inspect the source texture mode, verify baked alpha coverage and fixed-time record, then inspect the accessory in the final rendered model.
limitations: Static analog appearance only; no real-time clock or exact shader antialiasing equivalence. This is a scoped shader adaptation, not a universal MSDF or procedural-material baker.
